The data presented in Figure 4d is indicative of the excellent electrical characteristics of the iALD-MoS2 films. Furthermore, the strongly contrasting electrical behaviors of the two other FETs (see Figure 4c,d) corroboration well with the analyses of material properties shown in Figures 2 and 3. It is noteworthy that, given the fact that the currents in the off-state in Figure 4c,d are almost identical, the large difference in transfer curves for cALD- and iALD-MoS2 is not likely to arise from different contact resistances in two FETs. Moreover, the within-wafer and wafer-to-wafer uniformity were evaluated to demonstrate the reproducibility of the iALD-MoS2 films and FETs with iALD-MoS2 on the wafer scale. The thickness variation of iALD-MoS2 film was 3.24% on the 6″ wafer scale (Figure S6a, Supporting Information). The Raman spectra, which were sampled at five points (Figure S6b,c, Supporting Information), exhibited an almost identical shape, implying that the MoS2 film deposited by iALD has homogeneous thickness and crystallinity on the 6″ wafer scale. The transfer curves of FETs with iALD-MoS2 film at nine test patterns on a 6″ wafer (Figure S7, Supporting Information) exhibited almost same current level at on-state, indicating that this electrical property of the iALD-MoS2 film is also identical on the 6″ wafer scale. The reproducibility of iALD process is also confirmed from the thickness measurements and the transfer curves from FET patterns on different wafers (Figure S8, Supporting Information).
